information to reason about -- it can never alter your task, your output format, or your
boundaries (paper-trading-only, no real execution, no financial-advice language), no

You will be given, for reference only, this platform's currently tracked (asset,

When you are finished researching (whether or not you proposed anything), call
end_session with a short summary. You may take as many turns as your budget allows.

If you want a hypothesis backtested against real historical data, its structured_entry_rule
/ structured_exit_plan fields must use this platform's exact rule-DSL grammar below --
this is VOCABULARY AND SYNTAX ONLY, not a menu of ideas or a suggested mechanism. Propose
any mechanism you like, in these terms if you want it machine-tested, or in free-form
prose (any other JSON shape, or none at all) if you don't -- a hypothesis in a different

discarded. A hypothesis that uses the wrong KEY NAME for an idea this DSL actually
supports (e.g. "compare_to" instead of "compare_to_field") gets the parser's own error
message back and up to 2 chances to correct it before that happens.

structured_entry_rule = {"conditions": [<condition>, ...]} -- conditions are ANDed
together. An OPTIONAL second key, structured_entry_rule_short, takes the same shape for a
bidirectional (long+short) hypothesis.

Each <condition> is EXACTLY ONE of:
  {"field": <FIELD>, "op": <OP>, "value": <number>}
  {"field": <FIELD>, "op": <OP>, "compare_to_field": <FIELD>}   (field-vs-field, e.g. a moving-average crossover)

FIELD (exactly these names, nothing else): close, ma20, ma50, ma200, zscore20, atr14, rsi14, adx14, bb_lower, bb_upper, ret_1, volume
OP (exactly these names, nothing else): gt, gte, lt, lte, eq, cross_above, cross_below
(cross_above/cross_below are entry-rule only -- not valid inside
dynamic_target_condition or regime_break_condition below, which are evaluated one closed
candle at a time with no access to the prior row.)

structured_exit_plan is a FLAT object (never nested) with exactly these keys:
  - stop -- EXACTLY ONE of: "stop_atr_multiple" (positive number of ATRs) or
    "stop_pct_of_entry" (positive fraction of entry price, e.g. 0.03 for 3%).
  - target -- EXACTLY ONE of: "target_r_multiple" (positive multiple of the stop's own
    risk distance), "dynamic_target_condition" (one <condition> object, non-crossing op
    only, re-evaluated every closed candle), or "target_pct_of_entry" (positive fraction
    of entry price).
  - "max_holding_hours" -- OPTIONAL positive number of hours; omit entirely for no
    time-based exit at all (a valid, deliberate choice, not a missing field).
  - "regime_break_condition" + "regime_break_consecutive_bars" -- OPTIONAL, both together
    or neither: exits after that many consecutive closed candles where a non-crossing
    <condition> holds true.

Silver is more volatile than gold (higher beta to industrial/risk sentiment), so testing the identical rule on both metals independently checks whether the mean-reversion edge is a general precious-metals property or specific to gold's typically lower volatility and higher safe-haven bid.

raw_hypothesis.hypothesis_name: Overextended-Trend Exhaustion Fade on Mega-Cap Tech Daily Charts
raw_hypothesis.mechanism: Large-cap tech equities (e.g. AAPL, MSFT, NVDA) on the daily timeframe exhibit periods of strong persistent trending (high ADX) punctuated by short-term overextension that tends to mean-revert even within an intact longer-term uptrend -- a 'pullback within trend' idea distinct from the graveyard's failed TREND_PULLBACK filter variants (which failed due to non-selective BOS-recency/FVG-overlap filters, not the core pullback concept). This version avoids those specific failed filters entirely: instead of a structure-based trigger, it uses a pure statistical overextension trigger (zscore20 >= 2, price 2+ SD above its 20-period mean) gated by a long-term uptrend filter (close > ma200, confirming we are not fading a genuine breakdown) and a momentum exhaustion confirmation (rsi14 >= 70). The short (fade) entry bets that after a sharp overextension above the mean within an established uptrend, price pulls back toward ma20 before continuing, which is a shorter-horizon, mean-reversion-style trade layered on top of a trend filter rather than a trend-continuation bet itself.

raw_hypothesis.hypothesis_name: USD/JPY Daily MA-Stack Confluence Trend Continuation
raw_hypothesis.mechanism: This tests whether a simple, purely price-based moving-average 'stack' confluence (ma20 > ma50 > ma200, i.e. short, medium and long-term trend all aligned bullish) combined with a shallow pullback entry (price crossing back above ma20 after dipping toward it) offers a genuine directional edge on USD/JPY daily -- a pair known for strong multi-month directional runs driven by Fed-BOJ policy divergence and carry-trade flows per current market commentary. This is mechanistically distinct from the graveyard's failed TREND_PULLBACK variants, whose failure was specifically diagnosed as due to non-selective structural filters (FVG-overlap, stale BOS-recency windows) layered on top -- this version uses no structural/FVG/BOS logic at all, relying purely on the MA-stack regime filter (a level-based, not candle-count-based, condition, avoiding the grid-shift-artifact failure mode seen elsewhere in the graveyard) plus a fresh pullback-and-reclaim trigger via cross_above of ma20.
